findings.message: Case TDD.01.04.af07 bundles two structurally distinct AAA flows under one case ID: (a) a success-path assertion — 'claim returns COMMITTED only after the durable commit is observed, no write-behind' — which requires a healthy KV adapter in the Arrange phase; and (b) a failure-path assertion — 'commit failure → StoreUnavailableError, no orphan' — which requires a faulting KV adapter in the Arrange phase. These two flows cannot share a single Arrange block; they represent separate scenarios with different fixture states. A third concern is embedded: 'assert the durable-commit latency metric and a claim trace span (with status) emitted.' Combining two fixture states under one case ID means either the test function has multi-phase internal switching or the case ID implicitly covers two test functions with no ID-level distinguishability. Either form makes a failure non-diagnosable: a StoreUnavailableError assertion failure cannot be distinguished from an RPO assertion failure at the case-ID level.
findings.recommendation: Split TDD.01.04.af07 into two cases: (a) a success-path case asserting 'claim returns COMMITTED only after the durable commit is observed (RPO = 0), durable-commit latency metric and claim trace span emitted' — with a healthy KV adapter; (b) a failure-path case asserting 'commit failure → StoreUnavailableError, no orphan' — with a faulting KV adapter. Update §3 Test Mapping to list both new case IDs against the @bdd: BDD.01.03.8b97 row. The observability assertion (metric + trace span) belongs in the success-path case since it requires a completed commit to be observable.

findings.message: Case TDD.01.04.24ff asserts 'a KMS key-unwrap delay above the issuance budget (>200 ms) → claim completes within budget or raises StoreUnavailableError with no orphan.' The 200 ms threshold is stated as the KMS key-unwrap sub-component budget, but no upstream source (EARS, PRD, or SPEC) is cited for this specific value. SPEC §6 states the claim operation must complete 'within issuance budget EARS.01.03.f909 less commit headroom' but does not decompose that budget into a KMS-unwrap allocation. The 200 ms figure is unanchored: it may be an author assumption, a derived headroom estimate, or an implementation detail — none of those origins are declared. Without a citation the number is untraceable and cannot be gate-checked against the upstream NFR chain.
findings.recommendation: Either (a) cite the upstream source for the 200 ms sub-budget (e.g., if it is an author assumption, annotate it as such with '# author assumption pending SPEC §6 KMS sub-budget element' and flag for IPLAN binding), or (b) express the threshold in terms of the traceable budget: 'a KMS key-unwrap delay that causes total claim latency to exceed the EARS.01.03.f909 issuance budget → claim raises StoreUnavailableError with no orphan; the concrete ms ceiling binds at IPLAN when the KV provider is selected.' The IPLAN-defer pattern is already established in the artifact for cipher-mode and KMS key-ARN assertions (same case) and should be applied consistently to the latency threshold.

findings.message: The get-path degradation scenario (BDD.01.03.f44a) is encoded detection-only at the Link-Store boundary. Case 7115 asserts the failure is detected (StoreUnavailableError within 1 s, structured ERROR log) but no Link-Store case asserts the store's own recovery after the read path is restored. SPEC-01 §5 states the read-path error response as 'Surface StoreUnavailableError; redirect degrades fail-safe AND recovers when the store returns' — the 'recovers when the store returns' half is a Link-Store-level guarantee distinct from the Redirect Handler's own recovery. Detection-only encoding allows a store that latches into a permanently-failing read state (e.g. a stuck circuit breaker or cached unavailability) to pass the suite while never recovering, producing silent permanent degradation of the redirect hot path.
findings.recommendation: Add a paired recovery case in test_link_store_kv.py: inject the read-path fault, assert get raises StoreUnavailableError (detection, as 7115), then clear the injected fault via the controllable adapter/toxiproxy and assert a subsequent get resolves the known record within the p95 budget (recovery). This is the get-path analog of the ec06/4e51 detection+recovery pairs already present for the write paths.

findings.location: TDD-01 §4 Test Cases — Unit/Integration; cases cf05/54b8/1bc0 (get), 74e8/9528/ab25 (increment_visits)
findings.message: Input-fuzzing now covers the claim (8504) and set_status (fc47) code arguments with encoding-edge/injection classes, but two public-interface boundary inputs remain unfuzzed. (1) get(code) is exercised only on known/unknown/taken_down equivalence classes — no malformed/oversized/encoding-edge code (unicode NFC/NFD, percent-encoded, embedded NUL/control char, base62 homoglyph). A code that normalizes differently on the read path than on the claim path is a lookup-bypass / key-confusion surface at the trust boundary. (2) increment_visits(code, delta) has no fuzz on either argument — notably delta (negative/zero/overflow-width int), which can silently violate the SPEC §4 monotonic visit_count contract, and code on the same encoding-edge classes. Both are public Protocol methods that cross the substrate trust boundary, so per C2 each needs at least 1 fuzzing case.
findings.recommendation: Add a get-fuzz unit case (malformed/oversized/encoding-edge/homoglyph code -> ValueError before substrate read, or deterministic None, never a normalized-key collision with a claimed code) and an increment_visits-fuzz unit case (negative/zero/overflow delta rejected or no-op preserving monotonicity; encoding-edge code rejected before the native increment). Both belong in tests/unit/test_link_store.py, mirroring the 8504/fc47 input matrix.

findings.location: TDD-01 §4 test mapping row @adr: ADR.01.03.f5f5; ADR-01 §7 Rollback plan
findings.message: The one-way substrate decision ADR.01.03.f5f5 now has a deploy-gate smoke test (TDD.01.04.d5d7, type: smoke, timeout ≤30s, blocks all environments) — the forward deploy path is gated. However, no test exercises the rollback procedure in a non-prod environment. ADR §7 documents a seven-step runbook and step 7 explicitly requires an automated RPO = 0 smoke after the substrate re-point. TDD.01.04.d5d7 cannot serve as the post-rollback smoke: it commits a fresh code on the live substrate during the same run; it has no pre-imported records to verify as still-readable on the new substrate. The TDD suite therefore covers the forward deploy gate but leaves the post-rollback verification gate as an untested manual step.
findings.recommendation: Add a non-prod rollback-path integration test (e.g., TDD.01.04.rbXX, type: smoke, timeout ≤120s) that exercises at minimum steps 3, 5, and 7 of the ADR §7 runbook: (3) export a known set of committed records from the primary KV instance; (5) import them into a secondary KV instance with uniqueness-verification assertions (no duplicates, no data loss); (7) run an RPO = 0 probe against the secondary instance — claim a new code, then get verifies the pre-imported records still resolve. Tag it @adr: ADR.01.03.f5f5 and add it to the §5 smoke gate row alongside TDD.01.04.d5d7.

findings.location: §1 line 30 (cumulative upstream tags header) vs §3 lines 89-90 and §7 line 206
findings.message: Cumulative upstream tags header lists @adr: ADR-01 only, but §3 matrix rows 89-90 cite @adr: ADR.01.03.1050 and @adr: ADR.01.03.f5f5, and §7 line 206 expands to six ADR refs total: ADR-01 | ADR.01.03.5c3c | ADR.01.03.1050 | ADR.01.03.f5f5 | ADR.01.05.3afa | ADR.01.05.9107. The cumulative header is the artifact's traceability contract; it must enumerate every upstream element tag cited in the body.
findings.recommendation: Update line 30 cumulative upstream tags to include all element-level ADR refs: @adr: ADR-01 | @adr: ADR.01.03.5c3c | @adr: ADR.01.03.1050 | @adr: ADR.01.03.f5f5 | @adr: ADR.01.05.3afa | @adr: ADR.01.05.9107. Verify each tag resolves in the upstream ADR doc.

findings.location: TDD-01 §4 integration cases TDD.01.04.af07, TDD.01.04.840c; SPEC-01 §6 Observability paragraph
findings.message: SPEC §6 names 'atomic-claim outcome' as a distinct emission point, distinct from the write-conflict rate. TDD.01.04.840c verifies the conflict counter on a race; it does not assert a per-outcome labelled metric (e.g., a counter keyed {outcome=COMMITTED} or {outcome=CODE_TAKEN}) as implied by 'atomic-claim outcome' in SPEC §6. A missing outcome metric means the COMMITTED / CODE_TAKEN distribution is dark in production, which removes a first-order SLO signal.
findings.recommendation: Extend TDD.01.04.af07 to assert the atomic-claim-outcome metric is emitted with label outcome=COMMITTED on a successful claim, and add a companion assertion in TDD.01.04.82ff (unit, CODE_TAKEN path) or TDD.01.04.840c (integration, race path) that the outcome=CODE_TAKEN label variant is emitted. Cite @spec: SPEC-01 §6 on both assertions.

findings.message: The functional fault-injection cases cover network blip and registry-timeout scenarios from the application adapter's perspective. The remaining CI infrastructure failure mode is uncovered: (a) the KV substrate becomes unreachable during CI test-setup (not during a test operation) — the harness may silently skip or error the entire class rather than failing with an actionable message; (b) KMS / secrets-vault credential-fetch slowness during CI environment bootstrap exceeds the CI job timeout, producing a false timeout rather than a test failure. TDD.01.04.24ff covers a slow KMS response during a claim operation; the pre-test-setup credential-fetch timeout is a distinct unaddressed mode.
findings.recommendation: Add a CI pre-condition probe — a lightweight setup-phase check (not a test case) in the integration and e2e CI job configurations that asserts KV reachability and vault/KMS credential validity before the test runner starts. If the probe fails, the job exits non-zero with a structured error distinguishing 'infrastructure unavailable' from 'test failure'. Document this in a §5 note or CI appendix so the flake-budget accounting can correctly classify CI-environment failures separately from application flakes.
